questions.question: A 20 - page autobiography,’ Waiting for a Visa’, is written by ___________, which is about his experiences with untouchability.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar**, popularly known as **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, was a prominent **Indian social reformer, jurist, economist, and politician.**
 
• He is widely regarded as the **chief architect of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The 20-page autobiography titled **'Waiting for a Visa'** is a poignant account of Ambedkar's personal experiences with **untouchability** and caste-based discrimination.
 
• It details incidents from his life when he faced social ostracism and humiliation due to his caste, shedding light on the plight of the marginalized Dalit community in India.
 
• Ambedkar used his experiences as described in the autobiography to advocate for **social justice and equality**.
 
• 'Waiting for a Visa' serves as a significant document that highlights the harsh realities of the caste system in India and is often studied for its **sociological and historical importance**.
 
• Ambedkar's contributions include the drafting of laws to eradicate untouchability, his leadership in the Dalit movement, and his efforts to ensure **constitutional safeguards for marginalized communities.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule**__

 __
 
• **Jyotiba Phule** was a **social reformer** from Maharashtra and an activist for the upliftment of women and lower-caste communities.
 
• He is credited with founding the **Satyashodhak Samaj**, an organization aimed at promoting social equality.
 
• Phule also championed the cause of **education for women and Dalits**.
 
• Notable works of Jyotiba Phule include his **'Gulamgiri'**, which critiques the caste system.
 
 
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__
 __
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was an **Indian nationalist leader** and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was a mentor to **Mahatma Gandhi** and advocated for **moderate reforms** within the British colonial framework.
 
• Gokhale founded the **Servants of India Society**, which worked for the welfare of Indians under British rule.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**__
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the **Father of the Nation** in India, was a central figure in the **Indian independence movement.**
 
• His philosophy of **non-violence** (Ahimsa) and truth (Satyagraha) inspired movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
• Although Gandhi documented his experiences with untouchability in his writings, he did not author the autobiography titled **'Waiting for a Visa.'**

questions.question: Terekhol, Chapora, Mapusa, Sal, Zuari etc. are the major rivers of which state ?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Major rivers in Goa include the **Terekhol, Chapora, Mapusa, Sal, and Zuari**.
 
• The **Zuari River** is the largest river in Goa, and its basin covers a significant area of the state.
 
• Rivers in Goa play a vital role in **transportation, fishing, and agriculture**, supporting the local economy.
 
• Many of these rivers are connected to **backwaters**, creating scenic landscapes and attracting tourists.
 
• Goa's rivers are also home to rich **marine biodiversity**, including mangroves and various fish species.
 
• Several river cruises and water sports activities are hosted on these rivers, enhancing Goa's reputation as a **tourist destination.**
 
• The rivers hold cultural importance and are often associated with local **festivals and traditions.**

__
 
• **Telangana**__

 __
 
• Telangana is primarily drained by the **Godavari and Krishna rivers**, two major rivers of South India.
 
• These rivers play a crucial role in **agriculture and irrigation** in the region.
 
• Telangana is also home to **man-made reservoirs** and dams like Nagarjuna Sagar and Sriram Sagar.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh**__
 __
 
• Chhattisgarh is drained by the **Mahanadi River**, which is its largest river.
 
• The state is known for its rich **water resources**, with numerous tributaries like Seonath and Hasdeo flowing through it.
 
• The region hosts **hydroelectric projects** and irrigation systems that contribute to its economy.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__

• It is known for the **Sardar Sarovar Dam** on the Narmada River, one of India's largest dams.
 
• Rivers in Gujarat support agriculture, fisheries, and industries, playing a key role in the state's development.

questions.question: Which of the below mentioned items are NOT the part of revenue expenditure as per government budget?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Infrastructural Development Expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infrastructural Development Expenditure** is classified as a part of **capital expenditure** in the government budget.
 
• Capital expenditure refers to spending that leads to the creation of **assets** or **reduction in liabilities** and contributes to long-term growth.
 
• Examples of capital expenditure include building **roads, bridges, dams, and other infrastructure projects**.
 
• Such expenditures are considered investments that improve the country’s economic capacity over time.
 
• In contrast, **revenue expenditure** consists of recurring expenses that do not create any physical or financial assets, such as **salaries, subsidies, and interest payments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salaries and Pensions**__

 __
 
• **Salaries and pensions** are examples of **revenue expenditure** because they are recurring costs incurred by the government for running its administration and welfare functions.
 
• These expenses do not result in the creation of any physical or financial assets.
 
• They are essential for maintaining the functioning of government institutions and providing support to retired employees.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**__
 __
 
• **Subsidies** refer to financial support provided by the government to individuals, industries, or sectors to reduce their costs and make goods or services affordable.
 
• They are classified as **revenue expenditure** because they are recurring in nature and do not lead to asset creation.
 
• Examples include **food subsidies, fertilizer subsidies, and fuel subsidies**.
 
 
 
• **Interest Payments**__
 
 
• **Interest payments** are the cost the government incurs for servicing its debt obligations, including loans and bonds.
 
• They fall under the category of **revenue expenditure** because they are recurring and do not result in the creation of assets.
 
• This expenditure is critical for maintaining the government’s creditworthiness and financial stability.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts of the Indian Constitution facilitated the appointment of the same person as governor for two or more states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7th Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956** was a significant amendment to the **Indian Constitution** that brought about major changes in the political and administrative structure of India.
 
• This amendment facilitated the appointment of the **same person as governor** for two or more states.
 
• The provision for such appointments was included under **Article 153** of the Indian Constitution, which deals with the position of governors in states.
 
• The amendment was part of the reorganization of states in India, which aimed to address linguistic and administrative concerns.
 
• The objective was to ensure better coordination and efficiency in the administration of states, especially in cases where states were geographically proximate or shared common issues.
 
• It also aimed at reducing administrative expenses by appointing a single governor for multiple states where feasible.
 
• The **7th Amendment** is a landmark reform that contributed to the restructuring of states and the establishment of a more organized governance framework in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **5th Constitutional Amendment Act**__

 __
 
• The **5th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1955** focused on the procedures related to the reorganization of states.
 
• It amended **Article 3**, which lays down the process for the formation of new states or the alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• This amendment ensured that the views of the state legislature concerned are considered within a specified timeline.
 
 
 
• **8th Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 __
 
• The **8th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1960** dealt with the reservation of seats in Parliament and state legislatures for the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
• It extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs and special representation for the Anglo-Indian community for a further period of ten years.
 
 
 
• **10th Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 
 
• The **10th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1961** was enacted to incorporate the **territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli** into the Union of India.
 
• This amendment added **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** as a Union Territory under the First Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.question: Choose the correct group of greenhouse gases.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is **CH4, N2 O, CO2, O3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are responsible for trapping heat in the Earth’s atmosphere, leading to the **greenhouse effect**, which is a major contributor to **global warming** and **climate change**.
 
• The primary greenhouse gases in the Earth's atmosphere are **carbon dioxide (CO₂)**, **methane (CH₄)**, **nitrous oxide (N₂O)**, and **ozone (O₃)**.
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)**: Released through processes like **fossil fuel combustion**, **deforestation**, and **industrial activities**.
 
• **Methane (CH₄)**: A potent GHG emitted by sources such as **agriculture (e.g., rice paddies)**, **landfills**, and **livestock digestion (enteric fermentation)**.
 
• **Nitrous oxide (N₂O)**: Emitted from **agricultural soil management**, **fossil fuel combustion**, and some **industrial processes**.
 
• **Ozone (O₃)**: Acts as a GHG in the lower atmosphere (troposphere), although it is beneficial in the upper atmosphere (stratosphere) where it forms the **ozone layer**.
 
• The combination of these gases contributes significantly to the **Earth’s warming** by trapping heat radiated from the planet's surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CH₄, O₂, CO₂, N₂**__

 __
 
• This option incorrectly includes **oxygen (O₂)** and **nitrogen (N₂)**, which are not greenhouse gases.
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)** and **nitrogen (N₂)** are abundant gases in the atmosphere but do not trap heat significantly.
 
 
 
• **CH₄, O₂, CO₂, O₃**__
 __
 
• This option includes **oxygen (O₂)**, which is not a greenhouse gas.
 
• While the other gases listed (CH₄, CO₂, O₃) are greenhouse gases, the presence of oxygen makes this option incorrect.
 
 
 
• **H₂, O₂, CO₂, N₂**__
 
 
• This option incorrectly includes **hydrogen (H₂)** and **oxygen (O₂)**, which are not greenhouse gases.
 
• **Hydrogen (H₂)** is a potential clean energy source but does not contribute to the greenhouse effect.

questions.question: In which year did India's ‘National Food for Work Programme’ begin?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2004**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **National Food for Work Programme** was launched in **November 2004**.
 
• This programme was introduced by the **Government of India** to address **poverty and unemployment** in rural areas.
 
• The scheme aimed to provide supplementary food security and employment opportunities to the **most disadvantaged sections of society**.
 
• It was implemented in **150 of the most backward districts** in the country.
 
• The programme provided **unskilled manual work** to individuals in exchange for food grains as wages.
 
• The funding for this scheme was entirely from the **Government of India**, making it a **centrally sponsored programme**.
 
• The initiative was eventually subsumed under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2006**, which expanded the scope of rural employment and development.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a disadvantage of the green revolution?

options.text: High use of fertilisers and pesticides resulted in health illnesses.
Most of the crops introduced during green revolution were intensive crops.
It promoted extensive use of chemicals.
It reduced India’s import of food grains

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It reduced India's import of food grains.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution**, initiated in the 1960s, aimed to increase agricultural productivity in India through the use of **modern farming techniques, high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.**
 
• One of its major advantages was the **reduction in India's dependency on food grain imports**, enabling the nation to become self-sufficient in food production.
 
• India, prior to the Green Revolution, faced **frequent famines and food shortages**, often relying heavily on imports like wheat from countries such as the **United States**.
 
• Post-Green Revolution, there was a significant increase in the production of crops like **wheat and rice**, especially in states like **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh**, which led to a significant reduction in food grain imports.
 
• The Green Revolution not only ensured food security but also helped India to **export food grains** in subsequent years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **High use of fertilizers and pesticides resulted in health illnesses.**__

 __
 
• The extensive use of **chemical fertilizers and pesticides** during the Green Revolution led to a variety of health issues, including **skin disorders, respiratory problems, and even cancer**, especially in areas where these chemicals were used excessively.
 
• These chemicals also led to the contamination of **soil and water resources**, further aggravating the problem.
 
 
 
• **Most of the crops introduced during Green Revolution were intensive crops.**__
 __
 
• The focus of the Green Revolution was on **high-yielding variety (HYV) crops**, which required intensive care, including proper irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• These crops, while productive, were often resource-intensive and unsuitable for regions with limited agricultural resources.
 
 
 
• **It promoted extensive use of chemicals.**__
 
 
• The Green Revolution emphasized the use of chemical inputs like **synthetic fertilizers and pesticides** to enhance crop yields.
 
• While this increased productivity, it also resulted in **soil degradation, water pollution, and loss of biodiversity.**

questions.question: Terraces that are level on opposite sides of the valley are referred to as ______ terraces.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**paired**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paired terraces** refer to terraces that are **level and aligned on opposite sides** of a valley.
 
• They typically form due to **equal upliftment** of land and symmetrical erosion over time.
 
• Such terraces are often created during periods of **river incision**, where the river cuts into the landscape uniformly.
 
• Paired terraces are significant in **geomorphology** as they provide evidence for past **climatic conditions** and river activity.
 
• These terraces can be used to study the **chronology of river evolution** and changes in base levels.
 
• They are often associated with ancient floodplains or riverbeds that have been uplifted due to **tectonic activities**.
 
• Scientists use paired terraces to infer the **age and processes** of landscape formation in a region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Horizontal terraces**__

 __
 
• Horizontal terraces are generally **flat surfaces** formed due to sediment deposition over time.
 
• They are more associated with **agricultural activities** or geological formations resulting from slow sedimentary processes.
 
• Unlike paired terraces, horizontal terraces are not specifically aligned on opposite sides of a valley.
 
 
 
• **Symmetrical terraces**__
 __
 
• Symmetrical terraces refer to terraces that may appear **visually balanced**, but they do not necessarily align perfectly on opposite sides of a valley.
 
• They are often used in architectural or landscape design rather than geomorphological contexts.
 
 
 
• **Triangular terraces**__
 
 
• Triangular terraces are not a formal geomorphological term.
 
• They may refer to specific **shapes or formations** seen in landscapes but are not related to river incision or paired alignment.

questions.question: Which of these festivals commemorates the resurrection of Jesus from the dead?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Easter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Easter** is a Christian festival that celebrates the **resurrection of Jesus Christ** from the dead, as described in the New Testament of the Bible.
 
• The event is considered the **foundation of Christian faith**, as it signifies the triumph of Jesus over death and his role as the savior of humanity.
 
• Easter marks the end of the **Lenten season**, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance observed by Christians.
 
• The date of Easter varies each year as it is celebrated on the first Sunday following the **first full moon** on or after the spring equinox (March 21).
 
• It is often associated with various traditions, such as the **Easter egg**, which symbolizes new life, and the Easter bunny, which is linked to fertility and springtime.
 
• Easter is preceded by Holy Week, which includes important days such as **Good Friday** (commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus) and **Holy Saturday**.
 
• It is celebrated worldwide by Christians with church services, feasts, and cultural traditions, emphasizing the themes of **renewal, hope, and salvation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Good Friday**__

 __
 
• **Good Friday** is observed to commemorate the **crucifixion of Jesus Christ** and his death at Calvary.
 
• It is marked as a solemn day of mourning and reflection in Christianity, usually falling on the Friday before Easter Sunday.
 
• Church services on Good Friday often include the **Stations of the Cross**, veneration of the cross, and readings from the Gospel.
 
 
 
• **New Year**__
 __
 
• **New Year** is a global celebration marking the beginning of a **new calendar year**, based on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It is celebrated on **January 1** with festivities, fireworks, and resolutions for personal growth and improvement.
 
 
 
• **Christmas**__
 
 
• **Christmas** is celebrated on **December 25** to commemorate the **birth of Jesus Christ**.
 
• It is one of the most significant festivals in Christianity and is associated with traditions such as **gift-giving, decorating Christmas trees, and attending church services.**

questions.question: Rural Self - Employment Training Institute is an initiative of which Ministry of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rural Self-Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs)** are an initiative under the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India**.
 
• These institutes aim to provide **vocational training** to rural youth, enabling them to take up self-employment or wage employment opportunities.
 
• The program focuses on **skill development** to empower the rural population, especially those below the poverty line (BPL).
 
• The **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)**, a flagship program of the MoRD, supports RSETIs to enhance livelihood opportunities in rural areas.
 
• Each RSETI is typically set up in partnership with **banks and state governments**, ensuring a robust public-private collaboration.
 
• The training provided is **free of cost** and includes a variety of sectors such as **agriculture, business, and services** to cater to diverse employment needs.
 
• The initiative also emphasizes **hand-holding support** post-training to ensure the sustainability of self-employment ventures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Agriculture**__

 __
 
• The Ministry of Agriculture focuses on **agricultural development**, including crop production, irrigation management, and farmer welfare.
 
• It oversees programs like **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana** and **Soil Health Card Scheme**.
 
• While related to rural livelihoods, it does not directly manage **RSETIs**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Labour and Employment**__
 __
 
• This ministry is responsible for **policies related to employment, workforce welfare, and labor laws**.
 
• It implements programs like the **National Career Service** and **Employees’ State Insurance Scheme**.
 
• Its focus is more on the organized and unorganized workforce than rural self-employment training.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Finance**__
 
 
• The Ministry of Finance primarily deals with **fiscal policies, economic development, and financial regulations.**
 
• It oversees programs such as **PM Jan Dhan Yojana** and **Direct Benefit Transfers** to promote financial inclusion.
 
• Although it supports rural development indirectly through financial schemes, it does not operate **RSETIs**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Attorney General of India?

options.text: He / She can participate in sessions of the parliament.
He / She can vote in the Lok Sabha during the passage of confidence motion and no - confidence motion.
He / She cannot participate in joint sitting of the parliament.
He / She does not enjoy any immunity or privileges as compared to members of the parliament.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**He / She can participate in sessions of the parliament.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is the highest law officer in India and is appointed under **Article 76 of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• He/She is responsible for advising the government on legal matters and representing the Union Government in the Supreme Court and other courts.
 
• The Attorney General has the **right to participate** in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• However, while he/she can speak and participate in discussions in Parliament, the Attorney General does **not have voting rights** in parliamentary proceedings.
 
• The Attorney General enjoys certain privileges and immunities while performing their official duties but does not hold a seat in Parliament.
 
• This provision allows the Attorney General to contribute to legal discussions and ensure that the government is well-informed on constitutional and legal matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: He / She can vote in the Lok Sabha during the passage of confidence motion and no-confidence motion.**__

 __
 
• The Attorney General does **not have voting rights** in Parliament as he/she is not an elected member of either House.
 
• Voting rights are reserved for elected members of Parliament, such as MPs in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: He / She cannot participate in joint sitting of the parliament.**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect. The Attorney General has the **right to participate in all sessions** of Parliament, including joint sittings.
 
• However, as mentioned earlier, he/she cannot vote in these proceedings.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: He / She does not enjoy any immunity or privileges as compared to members of the parliament.**__
 
 
• The Attorney General enjoys certain **privileges and immunities** while discharging their official duties, similar to those granted to Members of Parliament.
 
• These include protection against legal proceedings for acts performed in their official capacity.

questions.question:
Consider the below mentioned statements and select the correct option with respect to the Indian folk and tribal dance forms:

i) Matki is the folk dance of Assam.

ii) Thang Ta is the folk dance of Manipur.

iii) Fugdi is the folk dance of Goa.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iii) are right.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Matki** is a folk dance, but it is not from **Assam**. It is a popular dance form of the **Malwa region in Madhya Pradesh**, performed by women carrying earthen pots (Matki) on their heads. Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.
 
• **Thang Ta** is a traditional martial art-based dance form of **Manipur**. It combines dance, martial skills, and rituals and represents a significant aspect of Manipuri culture. Hence, statement (ii) is correct.
 
• **Fugdi** is a folk dance of **Goa**, performed by women during religious and festive occasions. It is characterized by its fast rhythmic movements and circular formations. Hence, statement (iii) is correct.
 
• The correct option is that both **statements (ii) and (iii)** are accurate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Matki Dance**__

 __
 
• **Matki** is performed by women from the **Malwa region in Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It involves balancing an earthen pot (Matki) on the head while performing graceful movements.
 
• This dance form is often performed during celebrations like **festivals and weddings**.
 
 
 
• **Thang Ta**__
 __
 
• Thang Ta is a martial art form that is indigenous to **Manipur**.
 
• The term "Thang" refers to the sword, and "Ta" refers to the spear.
 
• It showcases the **valor and tradition** of Manipuri warriors, blending combat techniques with artistic expressions.
 
 
 
• **Fugdi Dance**__
 
 
• **Fugdi** is performed by the women of **Goa**, especially during the **Ganesh Chaturthi festival**.
 
• The dance is performed in a circular or serpentine formation and is accompanied by folk songs.
 
• It is a vibrant representation of **Goan culture**.

questions.question: The students in a physics lab have been asked to measure the amount of electric current in a circuit. Which device should they use?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ammeter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ammeter** is a device used to measure the **electric current** flowing through a circuit.
 
• The unit of current measured by an ammeter is **ampere (A).**
 
• An ammeter is connected in **series** with the circuit to ensure that the entire current passes through it for accurate measurement.
 
• The internal resistance of an ammeter is kept **very low** to avoid any significant alteration in the circuit's current.
 
• Ammeter is widely used in **laboratories, industrial applications, and electrical troubleshooting** to measure current.
 
• Modern ammeters often use advanced technologies like **digital displays** for precise readings.
 
• An ammeter is a fundamental tool in understanding and analyzing **electric circuits**, especially in academic settings like physics labs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Altimeter**__

 __
 
• An **altimeter** is an instrument used to measure **altitude**, i.e., the height above sea level.
 
• It is commonly used in **aeronautics, mountaineering, and navigation** to determine elevation.
 
• The device works based on **air pressure**, as air pressure decreases with altitude.
 
• It is not related to measuring electrical current and hence cannot be used in a physics lab for this purpose.
 
 
 
• **Ohmmeter**__
 __
 
• An **ohmmeter** is used to measure **electrical resistance** in a circuit.
 
• Its unit of measurement is the **ohm (Ω).**

• These substances are typically **non-biodegradable**, meaning they do not break down naturally in the environment, and thus accumulate in the tissues of organisms.

• This can occur in cases where the growth of organisms dilutes the concentration of pollutants in their bodies.
 
• It is a phenomenon often observed in **aquatic ecosystems** under certain conditions.

• Devaluation increases the competitiveness of a country's exports, making them more attractive in the **global market**.
 
• This step also discourages imports by making them more expensive, thereby helping in reducing the **trade deficit**.
 
• Devaluation is different from depreciation, which is a natural decline in the value of a currency due to **market forces**.

questions.question: When did humans become food producers in history?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neolithic Age Middle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neolithic Age**, also known as the **New Stone Age**, marked a revolutionary transition in human history from **hunting-gathering** to **food production**.
 
• During this period, humans began practicing **agriculture**, domesticating animals, and settling in permanent communities.
 
• The shift to food production occurred around **10,000 BCE** in some parts of the world, particularly in regions like the **Fertile Crescent** in the Middle East.
 
• Tools became more advanced, with the development of **polished stone tools** used for farming and other daily activities.
 
• Pottery was invented to store food and water, which was essential for settled agricultural life.
 
• Humans began cultivating staple crops such as **wheat, barley, rice, and millet**, depending on the geographical region.
 
• This age witnessed the rise of small villages and the beginning of a more organized social structure.
 
• The Neolithic Revolution laid the foundation for the development of **civilizations**, leading to advancements in technology, art, and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stone Age**__

 __
 
• The Stone Age is divided into three periods: **Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic**.
 
• During the **Paleolithic Age**, humans were primarily hunter-gatherers and used **basic stone tools**.
 
• The **Mesolithic Age** introduced more advanced tools and some early signs of food cultivation.
 
• However, large-scale food production was not characteristic of the Stone Age until the **Neolithic period**.
 
 
 
• **Paleolithic Age**__
 __
 
• The **Paleolithic Age**, or the Old Stone Age, primarily involved a lifestyle of **hunting and gathering**.
 
• Humans used rudimentary tools made of stone, wood, and bone.
 
• There was no evidence of organized agriculture or food production during this period.
 
• Humans were nomadic and depended on natural resources for survival.
 
 
 
• **Copper Age**__
 
 
• The **Copper Age**, also known as the **Chalcolithic Age**, marked the transition from the Stone Age to the Bronze Age.
 
• It was characterized by the use of **copper tools and weapons** but did not see significant advancements in food production.
 
• Humans continued agricultural practices initiated during the Neolithic Age.
 
• This age is often associated with the rise of early civilizations and more complex social structures.

questions.question: Vegetation that is completely Indian is called endemic or native species, while the plants that come from outside India are called ______.

__
 
• **Exotic species** refer to plant or animal species that are introduced to a region or country from outside their natural habitat or geographical area.
 
• These species are not native to the region and are often brought intentionally or unintentionally by **human activities**, such as trade, agriculture, or exploration.
 
• Examples of **exotic plants** in India include **Tea (Camellia sinensis)**, which originated from China, and **Eucalyptus**, which is native to Australia.
 
• Exotic species can sometimes adapt well to the new environment, but they may also disrupt the local ecosystem by competing with native species for **resources** or introducing **diseases**.
 
• In some cases, they are considered invasive when their growth and spread have detrimental effects on biodiversity, agriculture, or human health.
 
• Several laws and policies, such as the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, aim to regulate the introduction of exotic species in India to prevent ecological harm.
 
• Understanding the distinction between native and exotic species is crucial for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Native species**__

 __
 
• **Native species** are plants or animals that originate and thrive naturally in a specific geographical location.
 
• They are adapted to their local environment and contribute significantly to the **ecosystem's stability**.
 
• In India, examples of native plants include **Neem (Azadirachta indica)** and **Banyan (Ficus benghalensis)**.
 
• Native species are essential for preserving **biodiversity** and maintaining ecological balance.
 
 
 
• **Non-native species**__
 __
 
• **Non-native species** are similar to exotic species, as they originate from outside the region.
 
• However, they may not always become invasive or cause harm to the local ecosystem.
 
• Examples include **Potatoes** and **Tomatoes**, which were introduced to India from South America but are now widely cultivated.
 
 
 
• **Endangered species**__
 
 
• **Endangered species** are plants or animals at risk of extinction due to factors such as habitat loss, hunting, pollution, or climate change.
 
• India has many endangered species, including the **Bengal Tiger** and the **One-Horned Rhinoceros**.
 
• Efforts to protect endangered species include initiatives like the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, and the establishment of national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
